patterns.what_worked: Putting the pure half (the rotation run state machine, the grade bands, the contract accessors) in practice.lua made the whole engine offline-testable; the three operator corrections (the panel map, the registry reconciliation, the class-module lookup) were all resolved WITHOUT breaking a class suite once the reconciliation switched from 'retire the built-in' to 'keep it registered, delegate its grading, route the class to its own list'.
patterns.what_was_hard: The registry reconciliation: retiring the superseded built-ins was the literal reading of the ruling and it reddened three class suites (24 pins + 2 crashes) whose files are outside this lane's scope. The backward-compatible shape (all eight stay registered; the class list wins in the routing; the built-in's grading is delegated) satisfied the ruling and kept every class suite green.
patterns.skill_gap: The class-module lookup read the namespace table while the class tables live on the AceAddon table - a cross-module table split the offline sandbox hides (the sandbox keeps them apart; the client does not). The offline harness cannot catch that class of bug; a wiring check against the AceAddon table would.
